decision: Use one shared Qwen-compatible model endpoint for logical agents.
Never expose unrestricted shell or unrestricted SQL as tools.
Use deterministic verification as the success gate.
Implement inspect_vector as the only executable skill in Checkpoint 1.
Use an external Docker-managed named volume for persistent PostGIS storage and attach PostGIS declaratively to both the GeoServer default network and geoagent-backend.
Implement PostGIS validation as a deterministic read-only verifier, separate from LLM agents, using fixed SQL and validated identifiers.
Derive final workflow success exclusively from deterministic PostGIS validation and generate a secret-redacted JSON trace and Markdown report for every completed workflow.
Verify report and trace roots are writable before any database execution and block all artifact overwrites.
Build Planner Agent context deterministically from fixed trusted project files, include only implemented skills, bound context size, record source hashes, and redact secrets before model access.

Treat Planner Agent model output as untrusted JSON and require Pydantic schema validation plus deterministic skill, approval, ordering, validation, and no-execution policy checks before accepting a plan.

Run the Planner Agent in an independent non-root read-only container connected only to the model network, with read-only manifest and context mounts and no PostGIS credentials, GIS data, MCP execution access, artifact mounts, or Docker socket.

Bind every human approval to the SHA-256 digest of one canonical validated plan and an explicit set of approval-required step IDs; reject changed, expired, denied, incomplete, or overwritten approvals.

Translate only the exact approved four-step vector-to-PostGIS plan into one typed run_vector_postgis_workflow execution envelope; reject mismatched paths, targets, schemas, identifiers, arguments, approvals, skill order, or execution claims.

Use MCP Streamable HTTP only on the internal Docker control network, retain STDIO for local tests, publish no host port, restrict expected Host and Origin values, and keep write tools disabled by default.

Allow the Executor to call only one composite approval-gated MCP workflow; independently reload and verify the exact plan, approval, digest, envelope, schemas, and step scope inside the GIS container before controlled execution, and derive success only from deterministic validation.

Build the Critic context deterministically from trusted trace and report roots, enforce path and size limits, validate trace consistency, redact secrets, preserve evidence hashes, and treat incomplete evidence separately from validated success.

Run the Critic Agent as an independent non-root read-only container with model-network access only, read-only trace and report mounts, no MCP or PostGIS access, and deterministic policy that prevents the model from changing status or making unsupported success claims.

Separate GitHub-hosted CI into secret-free Python 3.12 offline tests and independent non-root container builds, while keeping Ollama, PostGIS, approval-gated execution, and other laptop-dependent integration tests outside hosted CI until a secured self-hosted runner is designed.

Represent model, MCP, execution, validation, cancellation, dependency, and internal failures using a stable secret-redacted taxonomy with deterministic exit codes and retry dispositions; permit retry only for explicitly safe read-only operations, require manual review for uncertain or interrupted database writes, and persist structured failure evidence in traces and reports.

Persist each workflow lifecycle as a schema-validated, secret-redacted state record with append-only transitions, monotonic revisions, atomic writes, exact plan and approval identity, and deterministic resume assessment; allow continuation only before execution begins, require manual review whenever a PostGIS write may have started, and expose state to the Executor through a read-only mount without implementing automatic retry or execution.

Manage versioned GeoAgent artifacts through one central schema registry, require explicit schema versions before Pydantic validation, fail closed on missing, invalid, unsupported older, and unknown future versions, write only the current registered version, and provide read-only compatibility and migration assessments without silently modifying or migrating artifacts.

Execute reusable recipes only through a typed SHA-256-bound recipe envelope, exact step-scoped human approval, and the fixed composite run_approved_recipe MCP tool; allow the independent Executor to call only health_check and the two approval-gated composite workflow tools, keep GIS libraries, data mounts, output writes, and credentials out of the Executor, independently reload and verify recipes, approvals, schemas, registry metadata, and envelopes inside the non-root GIS container, dispatch only hard-coded implemented skills, and derive recipe success from deterministic per-step validation.

Persist each completed approved recipe run inside the non-root GIS container as an immutable digest-addressed RecipeRunResult, cryptographic RecipeRunEvidence record, artifact-lineage manifest, and deterministic Markdown report; return the validated run result and durable references through a typed MCP response, independently verify the run-result digest and approved recipe identity inside the Executor, keep evidence storage and GIS output inaccessible to the Executor, prohibit overwrite and automatic replay, and require manual review whenever execution completes but durable persistence is incomplete.

Treat local-model output as an untrusted, non-executable RecipeProposal limited to fixed allowlisted templates; require schema validation, deterministic readiness assessment, trusted template compilation, recipe-policy validation, and an explicit operator save before the existing approval and execution boundaries. The model receives no shell, MCP, filesystem-write, database-write, approval, or execution authority.

Separate natural-language recipe review from persistent storage: generate and assess untrusted model proposals without writes, compile only fixed trusted templates, return clarification as a valid non-error outcome, render deterministic operator summaries, and permit immutable recipe storage only through a separate explicit command that reloads the review, verifies its schema, deterministically recompiles the proposal, and rejects any mismatch. Approval and execution remain separate later boundaries.

Generate new GIS skill skeletons only as isolated, non-overwriting, untrusted scaffold bundles; derive approval and validation requirements deterministically from skill access, keep generated registry entries planned with no executable entrypoint or verifier, validate bundles without importing generated code, and require separate human implementation, contract testing, and promotion before live registration.

Export only exact approved recipes into immutable digest-addressed Snakemake packages whose canonical Snakefile contains no shell rule and calls one trusted replay adapter; run Snakemake in a separate non-root control-network container with no model, GIS stack, PostGIS credentials, or direct output mount; independently revalidate the export, recipe, approval, digest, and step scope before invoking the existing Executor-to-MCP boundary, and write a completion marker only after deterministic validated success and durable evidence persistence.

Define standard GIS skills through versioned declarative YAML, fixed permission profiles, a trusted adapter catalog, immutable digest-addressed contracts, isolated untrusted scaffolds, trusted adapter materialization, network-disabled candidate tests, digest-bound test evidence, deterministic promotion assessment and exact promotion plans, and explicit transactional promotion with the trusted registry modified last. Declarative input, model output, generated scaffolds, and passing static contracts cannot inject executable code, grant permissions, modify the registry, or become trusted without the separate reviewed promotion boundary.

Extend hosted container CI beyond image-build and CLI-help smoke tests with deterministic container contracts: load all agent manifests in the real non-root agent image, perform read-only vector and raster inspection in the real GIS image, verify controlled rejection of raster path escape, require the isolated skill-test runner to fail closed without a valid candidate bundle, and validate Compose configuration. Run these contracts with no network, read-only root filesystems, dropped Linux capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only public fixtures, no model endpoint, no PostGIS credentials and no write-enabled integration execution.

Implement controlled raster transformation through a versioned declarative convert_raster definition bound to a fixed trusted Rasterio adapter and fixed trusted verifier; require artifact-write access, exact step-scoped approval, approved-root containment, symlink rejection, safe GeoTIFF target names, no overwrite, allowlisted resampling, temporary output creation, independent validation, and SHA-256 artifact lineage before final success. Extend trusted adapter metadata and promotion planning so every validation-required generated skill preserves an exact verifier identity; model output, declarative definitions and generated candidates cannot select arbitrary entrypoints or verifiers or promote themselves.

Define reusable recipe templates through one bounded, strictly validated, data-only YAML catalog containing only allowlisted parameter-profile identifiers, assessment-policy identifiers and deterministic step-graph data; generate proposal prompt contracts and WorkflowRecipe steps from that catalog while preserving strict trusted Pydantic parameter validation, registered-skill policy, approval, execution, validation, evidence and Snakemake boundaries. Reject symlinks, unknown fields, unsafe graph structure, arbitrary parameters and unknown templates; retain exact legacy parity checks for the original five templates during migration. Catalog data cannot provide Python, imports, entrypoints, verifiers, shell commands, SQL, permissions, approvals or execution claims, and new executable behavior still requires separately reviewed skill implementation and promotion.

Evolve the post-catalog prototype through an isolated Builder boundary, versioned spatial-data contracts, deterministic dirty-data benchmarks, correlated agent operational identities, separate immutable Critic records and digest-addressed release packages before production-oriented PostGIS promotion or GeoServer publication. Keep model-generated implementation candidates, proposals and operational summaries non-authoritative; require existing typed policy, exact approval, independent validation, evidence and explicit promotion boundaries. Productize the existing Snakemake replay and provide a guided read-oriented demonstration, while deferring operational memory until pilot use establishes reviewed facts, provenance, retention and deletion requirements.

Introduce the Builder first as a proposal-only logical agent with a fixed zero-authority manifest and strictly typed in-memory request and result contracts. Allow only bounded adapter, schema, policy, test, renderer and isolated catalog-entry proposals; enforce normalized relative paths, fixed destination prefixes, file-count and byte limits, exact request-to-proposal correspondence and immutable false claims for filesystem modification, tool use, testing, validation, approval, trust, promotion and execution. Do not provide Ollama access, candidate materialization, container write mounts or promotion authority in this initial slice.

Invoke the Builder through the existing shared OpenAI-compatible model client using a deterministic JSON-only prompt, temperature zero, the exact typed Builder request, recursive secret redaction and the required BuilderProposal schema. Accept only one JSON object that passes strict Pydantic validation and exact deterministic request-to-proposal policy matching; reject malformed, fenced, non-object, additional-file and authority-claiming output. Return only an in-memory BuilderGenerationResult, with no CLI exposure, source context contents, filesystem materialization, testing, validation, trust, promotion or execution in this slice.

Introduce the Builder container in two stages, beginning with a static manifest-validation service built from the existing hardened non-root agent image. Connect it only to the model network; mount only the Builder manifest read-only; retain a read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges and bounded tmpfs; and withhold MCP, PostGIS, secrets, project context, source mounts, data, evidence, approvals, outputs and candidate workspaces. Prove this boundary through hosted-CI-compatible static Compose tests before adding a bounded proposal command or request mount.

Accept Builder work only through one bounded typed JSON request loaded from an approved root. Reject unavailable, empty, oversized, symlinked, nested, non-regular, malformed and schema-invalid request files; expose generation through a builder-propose CLI that emits the validated in-memory result only to stdout; and preserve typed model-failure exit behavior. In the Builder container, mount only the exact request file and Builder manifest read-only, retaining the model-only network and withholding source, context, MCP, database, credentials, approvals, evidence, outputs and candidate workspace writes.

Accept Builder output for materialization only as an operator-saved, size-bounded, non-symlinked and schema-valid BuilderGenerationResult beneath an approved generation root; bind it to a canonical SHA-256 digest and materialize only its exact declared files through a trusted operator-side service into a new digest-addressed isolated candidate directory using atomic finalization. Persist a deterministic candidate manifest, verify that the source generation did not change during materialization, calculate the resulting candidate-tree digest and refuse existing destinations, path escapes and symlinks. Materialization grants no testing, validation, execution, trust or promotion status, and the Builder model container receives no writable candidate mount.

Require every materialized Builder candidate to pass deterministic static inspection before isolated testing: resolve it as a direct non-symlinked child of the approved candidate root, reject all nested symlinks, strictly validate BUILDER_CANDIDATE.json, bind the directory identity to the task and generation digest, require the actual file set to match the manifest exactly, verify every declared content digest, parse supported Python, JSON and YAML syntax without importing or executing candidate code, and verify that the complete candidate-tree SHA-256 remains stable throughout inspection. Static inspection is read-only and cannot claim testing, runtime validation, implementation trust, promotion or execution.

Extend the existing hardened skill-test runner with an explicit Builder-candidate mode while preserving its original skill-candidate behavior. Require exactly one supported manifest, validate BUILDER_CANDIDATE.json through the trusted schema, mount the exact candidate read-only with no network, extend only bounded candidate package paths needed for pytest, and emit typed task, generation and before-and-after candidate-tree digests with deterministic test counts. Accept Builder test evidence only from a bounded non-symlinked evidence root after repeating static inspection and confirming exact task, generation and candidate-digest identity, unchanged candidate content, successful tests, unavailable network and a read-only mount. Passing tests execute untrusted implementation code but do not constitute deterministic GIS validation, implementation trust, promotion or workflow execution.

Prepare Builder candidates for human review by assembling the exact schema-valid generation, candidate manifest, fresh static inspection and digest-bound isolated-test assessment into one typed package whose task, model, generation digest, candidate-tree digest, file paths and content digests must agree. Treat all candidate paths as proposed and unapproved, serialize the package deterministically, persist it through temporary staging and atomic finalization in a new digest-addressed review directory, reject symlinked roots and existing packages, and verify stable candidate content before and during persistence. Review-package creation grants no human approval, trusted writes, implementation trust, promotion or execution authority.

Represent Builder human review as a separate typed approved or rejected decision bound to the exact immutable REVIEW.json digest. Require a unique decision ID, reviewer identity, timezone-aware timestamp, rationale and explicit path selection; permit approved paths only as a subset of reviewed proposals, and prohibit rejected decisions from selecting paths or authorizing promotion planning. Securely reload and verify canonical review content and its digest-addressed directory, then persist the decision separately as canonical DECISION.json through temporary staging and atomic finalization in an immutable digest-addressed directory while rechecking the review package. A recorded approval authorizes only later promotion planning and does not copy files, modify registries, establish implementation trust, promote code or execute workflows.

Allow Builder promotion planning only from a canonical immutable DECISION.json record whose digest-addressed directory, approved-root containment, schema and byte representation are verified. Require an approved human decision that explicitly authorizes planning, reload and verify its exact immutable review package, repeat candidate inspection, and bind the resulting non-writing plan to the review, decision, generation and candidate-tree digests. Map only explicitly approved reviewed paths, verify each source against the candidate manifest digest, reject missing files, symlinks, path escapes and existing destinations, and rehash the candidate after planning. Promotion planning creates no directories, copies no files, modifies no registry, establishes no trust and performs no execution.

Persist Builder promotion plans only as canonical immutable PLAN.json evidence after repeating the complete read-only promotion assessment. Bind each plan directory to the task ID and exact canonical-content SHA-256; use temporary staging and atomic finalization; reject symlinked roots, directories and files, malformed or noncanonical content, digest-directory mismatches, changed planning inputs and existing destinations; and securely reload plans only from their approved root. Expose persistence through create-builder-promotion-plan while preserving false file-copy, registry-modification, implementation-trust, promotion and execution claims. Approval and plan persistence authorize neither silent installation nor execution; transactional promotion remains a separate explicit operation.

Promote an approved Builder candidate first into one immutable digest-addressed bundle rather than writing multiple files directly into trusted source and test directories. Require exact operator confirmation of the decision ID and persisted promotion-plan SHA-256; securely reload the canonical PLAN.json; repeat the complete decision, review, candidate and destination assessment before and after staging; copy only explicitly approved files beneath files/<approved-destination-path>; verify source and staged SHA-256 digests; write canonical PROMOTION.json; and finalize the complete bundle through one atomic directory rename. Bundle promotion does not perform independent post-promotion verification, activation, registry modification, implementation trust or execution. This avoids falsely claiming that multiple cross-directory trusted-source writes can be finalized through one atomic filesystem operation.

Require independent digest-bound verification before any promoted Builder bundle can enter activation review. Securely reload the canonical promotion manifest and immutable PLAN.json, bind task, decision, plan, candidate-tree and directory identities, reject symlinks and file-set differences, verify every promoted-file SHA-256 twice, and detect changes during verification. Persist successful verification only as canonical digest-addressed VERIFICATION.json evidence after repeating verification before and during atomic storage. Verification and evidence persistence do not activate files, modify the registry, establish implementation trust or execute candidate code.

Require a separate immutable human activation-review decision after Builder promotion verification and before activation planning. Securely reload canonical VERIFICATION.json evidence, independently reverify the current promoted bundle, and bind each decision to the verification, promotion-plan and candidate-tree digests, exact promotion directory and complete reviewed file set. Treat the verified atomic bundle as all-or-nothing during activation review. Persist decisions only as canonical digest-addressed ACTIVATION_DECISION.json evidence after repeating verification before and during atomic storage. Approval authorizes only later activation planning and does not copy trusted-source files, modify the registry, activate the bundle, establish implementation trust or execute candidate code.

Require a separate non-writing Builder activation plan after immutable activation-review approval and before any trusted-source mutation. Securely reload the canonical ACTIVATION_DECISION.json and VERIFICATION.json evidence, independently reverify the promoted bundle, reload its canonical promotion manifest, bind all task, decision, verification, promotion-plan, candidate-tree, directory and file identities, verify every source digest, and require every trusted destination to be contained beneath the project root and absent. Persist plans only as canonical digest-addressed ACTIVATION_PLAN.json evidence after recreating the complete plan before and during atomic storage. Activation planning does not copy files, modify the registry, activate the bundle, establish implementation trust or execute candidate code.

Permit trusted-project Builder activation only from canonical immutable ACTIVATION_PLAN.json evidence with exact operator confirmation of the activation-decision ID and activation-plan SHA-256. Recreate the complete plan before mutation, refuse existing destinations, verify every promoted source digest, stage exact bytes beside each destination, reverify the evidence chain after staging, atomically rename each file, verify installed digests, and finalize canonical ACTIVATION.json evidence only after successful installation. On failure, remove only files created by that activation and clean temporary staging. Activation does not modify the registry, execute activated code, claim post-activation verification or establish implementation trust.

Establish Builder implementation trust only through a separate deterministic post-activation verifier. Securely reload canonical ACTIVATION.json, ACTIVATION_PLAN.json, activation-review and promotion-verification evidence; independently reverify the promoted bundle; bind all activation, plan, decision, verification, candidate-tree and project identities; require exact manifest-to-plan mappings; reject unexpected evidence entries, missing installed files, path escapes and symlinks; and hash every installed file twice. Persist successful trust results only as canonical digest-addressed POST_ACTIVATION_VERIFICATION.json evidence after repeating verification before and during atomic storage. Post-activation verification may set implementation_trusted true but does not modify the registry or execute implementation code.

Implement the presentation-required vector portion of spatial-data contracts as a separate deterministic read-only boundary. Require strict versioned schemas, bounded non-symlinked JSON or YAML loading beneath an approved contract root, canonical contract SHA-256, and stable before-and-after physical dataset digests. Assess CRS, allowed and mixed geometry types, required fields and logical types, null thresholds, unique keys, feature-count bounds, invalid, empty, null and duplicate geometries, and expected or permitted extent. Return typed checks and violations whose deterministic outcomes alone define pass status. Expose the operation through the operator CLI and the read-only MCP allowlist while granting no additional agent authority, filesystem mutation, database mutation, approval, workflow execution or model authority. Maintain a generated dirty-vector benchmark with explicit expected failures; defer raster contract fixtures until after the presentation-focused vector scope.

Represent agent operational history as strict versioned, append-only, correlation-scoped JSONL events with trusted role, instance, run, task, correlation and parent-run identities. Generate unique identities only in trusted code; require contiguous per-run sequences, monotonic aware timestamps and SHA-256 predecessor chains; bound event and log sizes; lock and durably append only beneath an approved non-symlink root; and revalidate the complete history on every load and append. Derive Planner, Executor, GIS-workflow and Critic events only from validated typed results or independently verified evidence. Keep Critic assessment separate from authoritative deterministic workflow status, record incomplete approval evidence without overstating success, and prohibit credentials, secrets, unrestricted prompts and private model reasoning. Model-agent containers receive no operational-history write authority.

Create authoritative workflow releases only from deterministic validated candidates whose exact plan, approval, trace, report, separately persisted Critic result and operational history are securely reloaded and mutually consistent. Bind every physical component by project-relative path, size and SHA-256; persist the canonical readiness assessment as CANDIDATE.json; bind it from canonical RELEASE.json; copy exact evidence beneath files/; verify sources before and after staging; and finalize the complete digest-addressed package through one atomic directory rename. Refuse non-ready candidates, replacement of a release ID, path escapes, symlinks, missing or unexpected entries, changed inputs and tampered packages. Independent inspection must revalidate candidate, manifest, directory identity, exact file set and every component digest without modifying files, executing workflows, changing authoritative status or modifying registries. Recipe-specific release assessment remains a later extension.

Bound the model-facing CURRENT_STATUS.md excerpt independently of the trusted source-file size so growth in durable project history cannot exhaust the local model context window. Preserve deterministic head and tail sections, include an explicit truncation marker and warning, and retain the SHA-256 reference of the complete unmodified source file. Keep project summary, architecture, selected datasets, implemented skills and relevant accepted decisions as separate trusted context fields.

Define the Checkpoint 14F pilot as one fixed presentation-focused vector scenario with a strict repository-owned demo definition, deterministic dirty and clean contract cases, and an exact workflow dataset bound by physical SHA-256. Require a read-only readiness gate before proposal; preserve separate model proposal, deterministic compilation, exact human approval, isolated execution, deterministic validation, correlation-scoped operational history, Critic evidence and authoritative release boundaries; and demonstrate Snakemake first through static validation and a no-output dry-run, followed only by explicitly approved replay while MCP writes are temporarily enabled and restored to disabled. Keep generated approvals, evidence, outputs, histories, Critic records, releases and replay packages outside Git. Treat new timestamps, IDs and digests as expected per run and make no claim that the vector pilot supplies deferred raster contracts, production promotion or publication.

Adopt ActionCharter as the public project and Python distribution name to reflect a domain-independent governed execution harness for AI agents using professional tools. Retain geoagent_harness, geoagent, geoagent-mcp, existing evidence fields and internal GeoAgent type names as 0.1.x compatibility interfaces. Present GIS as the first complete reference domain rather than the platform boundary, license the public project under Apache-2.0, and attribute the work to Jay Qi.

Preserve the existing v0.8.0 GeoAgent Skill Harness milestone tag as part of the continuous ActionCharter project history and publish the first ActionCharter public alpha as v0.9.0 rather than restarting at v0.1.0. Supersede only the 0.1.x compatibility-series wording in D-055 with 0.9.x; retain the adopted public identity, legacy import and CLI compatibility surfaces, Apache-2.0 license and authorship decision unchanged.

Introduce bounded PostGIS inspection as a read-only Checkpoint 15A control surface. Accept only conservative schema and table identifiers, require the schema to be allowlisted, and expose no SQL, predicates, ordering, joins or connection parameters. Use fixed catalog and aggregate queries through a read-only connection with a statement timeout; cap columns, keys, geometry columns and observed geometry types; and redact all connection failures. Return strict versioned metadata for relation existence, columns, primary and unique keys, geometry registration, CRS, observed geometry types, row and geometry-quality counts, and extent. Expose the same operation through CLI and the fixed MCP allowlist without granting mutation, approval, export, staging, promotion or publication authority.

Implement Checkpoint 15B PostGIS comparison only as a deterministic composition over the bounded 15A inspection boundary. Inspect two distinct, exact, allowlisted relations through one shared repeatable-read transaction; normalize constraint identity by key columns rather than table-specific constraint names; and compare columns, primary and unique keys, row count, geometry registration, CRS, observed geometry types, quality counts and extent. Return strict versioned matched or different status with bounded typed differences, using exit code one for valid differences and exit code two when evidence is unavailable or policy is denied. Expose no SQL, predicates, joins, tolerances, mutation, approval, export, staging, promotion or publication authority.

Classify Checkpoint 15C PostGIS change only from validated 15B comparison evidence using fixed deterministic policy. Treat column, primary-key, unique-key, geometry registration, CRS, declared-type and observed-type changes as incompatible; treat row-count, null or invalid geometry count, and extent changes as review-required when no incompatible change exists; and treat no differences as compatible. Structural incompatibility must dominate simultaneous observational drift, and unknown future differences must fail closed as incompatible. Return bounded typed findings and prohibit custom policy overrides, model judgment, approval creation, promotion authorization, arbitrary SQL and database mutation. Expose assessment through CLI and the read-only MCP allowlist without granting execution authority.

Plan Checkpoint 15D PostGIS promotion only from a fresh compatible assessment of two exact allowlisted relations in one repeatable-read transaction, while also proving that a distinct exact archive relation is absent. Bind the assessment and reference and candidate inspection snapshots by canonical SHA-256 into a strict non-executing plan. Fix the future choreography to assessment reverification, relation locking, archive-absence verification, reference archival, candidate promotion and post-promotion validation in one rollback-required transaction; require approval for exactly the two rename mutations. Accept no SQL, create no approval and perform no database mutation. Defer approval persistence and promotion execution.

Record Checkpoint 15E PostGIS promotion approval only after loading a bounded 15D plan-result file beneath an approved root and recomputing the canonical plan SHA-256. Persist the human decision as a canonical immutable digest-addressed package bound to the plan ID, plan digest, assessment digest and exactly the archive-reference and promote-candidate mutation steps. A denied decision approves no steps, and an approved decision containing corrections must fail closed until a replacement plan is generated. Redact operator text, permit optional future expiration, reject path escapes, symlinks, digest changes, duplicate package identity and noncanonical stored evidence, and perform no promotion or database mutation.

Execute PostGIS promotion only from an exact verified 15D plan and unexpired approved 15E decision with explicit confirmation of both digests and write tools enabled. In one serializable transaction, lock and reverify reference and candidate snapshots, prove the archive remains absent, perform only the fixed reference-to-archive and candidate-to-reference renames, validate the promoted relation before commit, and roll back every failure. Persist successful execution as canonical immutable digest-addressed evidence; accept no arbitrary SQL or model authority.
